text.p: England captain Tony Adams played his first competitive match on Tuesday since revealing his struggle against alcoholism, lasting a full 90 minutes for Arsenal reserves against minor league Welling United.

The 29-year-old defender, who has not represented Arsenal in the league since January following the first of two knee operations, last played in front of 80,000 supporters against Germany in the semifinals of Euro 96.

Barely 800 watched his comeback, which began inauspiciously when he stepped off the team coach before the game in front of a liquor store named `Squiffy's', attached to the main entrance of the ground.
Adams has admitted it was defeat by the Germans at Wembley in a penalty shoot-out which led to his drinking spiralling out of control.

He has also had other major problems in his private life, and is currently involved in divorce proceedings following revelations of his wife Jane's cocaine addiction. He was also jailed for two months in December 1990 for a drink-related motoring offence.
